title: Iktomi and the Ducks
text:
In a Dakota tale retold by Zitkala-Sa, Iktomi the trickster was walking along the edge of a lake with a bundle of grass tied on his back. A flock of ducks called out to ask what he was carrying. Iktomi said it was a bundle of songs.

The ducks begged him to sing them some. Iktomi agreed. He built a lodge of grass on the shore, and all the ducks crowded inside. He would sing, he told them, and they must dance with their eyes shut tight.

The ducks danced with their eyes closed. As they circled past him, Iktomi reached out, grabbed one, and wrung its neck, then another, still singing. The ducks heard nothing but the song and kept dancing.

Finally a little duck opened one eye a crack. He saw what was happening and screamed for the others to run, because Iktomi was killing them. The survivors fled out of the lodge and into the water.

Iktomi roasted his catch anyway. But while the ducks were cooking, he climbed a tree to stop two branches from creaking and got himself stuck between them, and a pack of wolves came by and ate every duck, leaving him only the bones.
lesson: A group that follows orders with its eyes shut can be picked off one at a time. Value the member who looks and speaks up, even if it means breaking ranks.
location: Dakota lands, northern Great Plains, United States
source: Zitkala-Sa, Old Indian Legends (1901), Iktomi and the Ducks
